questions.question: What is the difference between structural and attribute directives in Angular?
questions.title: Structural vs Attribute Directives in Angular — Differences
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between structural and attribute directives in Angular?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Structural directives change DOM layout (*ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch); attribute directives change appearance/behavior (ngClass, ngStyle, custom).

**Classic weak answer:** Applying two structural directives to the same element — not allowed; use a wrapper ng-container.

**Senior finish:** Mention the new Angular 17+ control flow syntax (@if, @for, @switch) that replaces *ngIf/*ngFor.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Structural vs Attribute Directives in Angular — Differences** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the difference between structural and attribute directives in Angular?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Structural directives change DOM layout (*ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch); attribute directives change appearance/behavior (ngClass, ngStyle, custom)**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Applying two structural directives to the same element — not allowed; use a wrapper ng-container**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention the new Angular 17+ control flow syntax (@if, @for, @switch) that replaces *ngIf/*ngFor**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Structural directives change DOM layout (*ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch); attribute directives change appearance/behavior (ngClass, ngStyle, custom)
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **applying two structural directives to the same element — not allowed; use a wrapper ng-container** and what you do instead.

questions.question: What is the new Angular 17+ control flow syntax (@if, @for, @switch)?
questions.title: Angular 17 Control Flow — @if, @for, @switch (Replacing *ngIf/*ngFor)
questions.direct_answer:
What is the new Angular 17+ control flow syntax (@if, @for, @switch)?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Built-in @if/@for/@switch blocks, tracking with track, @empty blocks, faster and ergonomically better than *ngIf/*ngFor.

**Classic weak answer:** Still using *ngIf/*ngFor in new Angular 17+ code — the new control flow is faster and recommended.

**Senior finish:** Highlight that Angular CLI includes a migration schematic; new syntax gives better type narrowing and perf.
